An den Frühlingstagen ziehen geschmückte: On the spring days decorated barges sail past the lighthouse. Fish smokes on the Salt Market, and the Salt Queen takes her seat on her throne of barrels. Anyone who can weave wreaths is welcome at the Buoy Innkeeper's.
Die Hunde sind schneller als die Constab:
The dogs are faster than the constables, but the Crater Forest is no friend of theirs at night. You run until the lanterns behind you are only sparks.

At the canal Kit throws the tarpaulin over you and pushes off without asking. "Price asked the whole Night Market about you," he says after a while. "No one said anything. Not yet."
Du läufst vom Baustellenzaun bis zum Güt:
You run from the building-site fence to the freight yard without turning around. No one follows you. That is the eeriest part.

On the ticket, in tiny writing, is a second note: "Wexmoor. Ask about the light." The train slows down. It doesn't stop.
Dunscar feiert an den Sommertagen den Sc: Dunscar celebrates the shift change on the summer days: brass music on the Sleeper Ring, pay packets, beer from the barrel and a boxing ring of ropes in the lime dust. The railway runs no tubs that day.
Im Morgengrauen klebt Price den ersten s:
At dawn Price pastes up the first one himself. By noon every lamppost between the Old Market and the North Gate carries the same sheet: your face, neatly drawn, and below it in block letters "Wanted. Fivefold embezzlement of evidence. Grievous bodily harm to Professor L. Starling. Suspected complicity in the cases of Ashgrove Lane, North Gate, the foundry, Villa Ashcombe and St. Brigid. Fifty shillings."

The people you saved read it and look away. Constables walk their beats. Whoever sees you reports it to Price.
In den Nächten dieses Herbstes hängt Ket: On the nights of this autumn Kettlegate hangs paper lanterns in the alleys. A stage stands on the Old Market, candle boats drift down the canal. The watch asks that fire baskets not be left unattended.
Kit kennt den Güterbahnhof besser als di:
Kit knows the freight yard better than the railway does. You wait between two coal wagons until the shunter's lamp has passed. "You'll come back, won't you?" he asks, and doesn't wait for the answer.

The train to Wexmoor doesn't stop in Kettlegate. It only slows down. That's enough.
Lantern Night on the autumn nights.
Marlowe bringt dich selbst zum Güterbahn:
Marlowe takes you to the freight yard herself, in the service car, under a blanket. She doesn't say a word the whole way.

At the track she presses the ticket into your hand. "I read Starling's letters. Every sentence twice. The bad thing isn't that they lie. The bad thing is how well they do it." The train to Wexmoor slows down. It doesn't stop.
Marlowe hält Price auf der Treppe auf, u:
Marlowe holds Price up on the stairs, and you slip out the back door into the Crater Forest. Behind you, you hear him roaring that Starling's blood is still on your hands. It is light, not blood, but in the dark no one can tell.

Three hours. You don't take the way through the city. You take the canal, where Kit is waiting with the coal barge, because Marlowe gave him a shilling and a look.
Salt Blessing on the spring days.
Shift Change on the summer days.
„Da ist er! Festhalten!“\n\nZwei Constab:
"There he is! Hold him!"

Two constables press you against the wall of a house; one holds the wanted poster next to your face and nods. At the station Price has you locked in the rearmost cell and goes looking for Marlowe to show her whom he has caught.

He doesn't find her. She finds you: at night, with the key to the yard. "That was the last time." Whatever was in your pockets stays in the evidence room. You come to under the Crow Bridge.
